newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower, awaits Fed rate move.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower, awaits Fed rate move.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar finished slightly lower in dull trade on Tuesday, marking time before the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee.
The currency closed at US$0.6956/63 and 68.35 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6968/75 and 68.41 at the opening.
Dealers said the morning session saw a partial continuation of the short squeeze that had carried the Kiwi up to 0.6977 overnight.
"The shorts were still trying to get their Kiwi back, but most of the activity today was just small sellers, and they brought it down towards that 0.6955 level," a trader said.
The range on the day was 0.6956-72.

A Wellington dealer said the expectation of a 25 basis point rise in the Federal Funds rate to 5.50 percent was built into currency markets. A 50 basis point rise could see the Australian and New Zealand dollars sold quite sharply.

"If they don't hike, the U.S. dollar itself could well come off quite a lot, now that's obviously going to be supportive for the Kiwi and the Aussie -- both currencies will gain a reasonable amount of support," he said.
Another dealer said a U.S. rate hike would slightly narrow New Zealand's interest rate differential but not to the point where the Kiwi became a big sell.
The likely overnight range was seen as 0.6950-75.
